title: A quasi-affine flat monomorphism has a quasi-affine open neighbourhood
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact flat monomorphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Monomorphism means that postcomposition with $f$ is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(W,X)$ for every scheme $W$. Suppose that $X$ is quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-open-immersion], and that $T$ is quasi-separated, meaning that the intersection of any two affine opens of $T$ is quasi-compact. Then there exists a quasi-compact quasi-affine open subscheme $U\subseteq T$ such that $f(|X|)\subseteq|U|$. Neither local finite presentation of $f$ nor a Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: §3, Proposition 3.4 (heading OCR 3.5), printed pp.14–15, proved using the following two lemmas. Its quasi-affine convention is quasi-compact open in an affine scheme. Primary scan: https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf . Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Put $E=f(|X|)$. It is quasi-compact, since $X$ is quasi-compact and $f$ is continuous, and stable under generalization by [lem-sfb-proopen-global-section-extension]. Fix $y\in E$ and $x\in X$ with $f(x)=y$, and choose an affine open $A\subseteq T$ containing $y$. Apply [lem-a1-quasi-affine-open-principal-comparison-cover] to the open immersion $f^{-1}(A)\hookrightarrow X$. Its principal comparison cover supplies $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ such that $x\in X_a\subseteq f^{-1}(A)$ (and $X_a$ is affine).

source.place: §3 Proposition 3.4 (heading OCR 3.5), printed pp.14–15; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proopen-global-section-extension] to $f$ and $a$. Obtain a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq T$ containing all of $E$ and $g\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ with $f_V^*g=a$. Local homomorphisms of local rings reflect units, so $f^{-1}(V_g)=X_a$. Consequently $y\in V_g$ and $E\cap V_g\subseteq A$.

source.place: §3 Proposition 3.4 (heading OCR 3.5), printed pp.14–15; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Set $F=V_g\setminus A$. Both $V_g$ and $V\cap A$ are quasi-compact opens of the quasi-separated scheme $V$: cover $V$ by finitely many affines, on which $V_g$ is a principal affine open; use quasi-separatedness for their intersections with $A$. Quasi-compact opens in a quasi-separated scheme are retrocompact, by intersecting their finite affine covers. Thus $F$ is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The qcqs scheme $V$ is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. If $e\in E\cap\overline F$, [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-proconstructible-closure-specialization], applied to the one-member family $F$, gives $z\in F$ with $e\in\overline{\{z\}}$. Generalization stability of $E$ then gives $z\in E$, contrary to $F\cap E=\varnothing$. Therefore $N=V\setminus\overline F$ is an open containing $E$. Cover $E$ by finitely many affine opens contained in $N$ and let $W$ be their union. The open $W_{g|W}=W\cap V_g$ is quasi-compact (on a finite affine cover of $W$, it is a principal affine open) and lies in $A$, since $W$ avoids $F$. It is therefore a quasi-compact open of the affine scheme $A$, hence quasi-affine by definition. It contains $y$, since $y\in E\cap V_g$.

source.place: Tag 0903, lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed (1), giving Raynaud Proposition 3.4 final constructible shrinking on printed p.15. Spectrality: properties.tex Tag 094L, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral.

proof.text: For every $y\in E$ the preceding construction gives a quasi-separated open $W\subseteq T$ containing all of $E$ (quasi-separatedness is inherited by opens), and a global function $g|W$ whose quasi-affine basic open contains $y$. These are exactly condition (ii) of [lem-sfb-quasiaffine-principal-neighbourhood-criterion]. Its implication (ii) to (i) gives a quasi-compact quasi-affine open $U\subseteq T$ containing $E$. If $X$ is empty, take $U=\varnothing$; it is the spectrum of the zero ring. No finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis was used.
